title: 1999 AMC 8 Problem 22
statement: In a far-off land three fish can be traded for two loaves of bread and a loaf of bread can be traded for four bags of rice. How many bags of rice is one fish worth?

solutions.text:
Three fish are worth two loaves of bread, so one fish is worth \(\dfrac23\) of a loaf.

One loaf is worth \(4\) bags of rice, so one fish is worth \(\dfrac23\cdot4=\dfrac83=2\dfrac23\) bags of rice.

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Turn each trade into a value equation
Convert fish to bread, then bread to rice
